transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-04 09:30 UTC • Duration: 45m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Sara Gomez (BluePeak Head of ML), Anil Patel (BluePeak DevOps), Karen Li (BluePeak CTO)

Summary: quick sync on pilot status — networking items blocking peering, latest perf numbers after SE tuning, and upgrade plan.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, quick check-in today. We'll go through the network ask, the benchmark results that Liam pushed yesterday, and then the upgrade timing. Sara, can you kick off with where things are on your side?

[00:18] Sara: Yeah, sure. Thanks Maya. Um, so overall the inference tests looked better after the KV cache change Liam suggested. We're seeing average p95 latency drop from, like, 520ms to roughly 310ms on the 8k token sim, which is promising. There is some jitter though on cold-start, and the cross-AZ failover test still shows an extra 200–300ms hit.

[00:42] Liam: Right, that's consistent with what we expected. The KV cache warm-up and the continuous batching tweak helped reduce per-token overhead. We also bumped the batch size from 8 to 12 for that workload which helped throughput but increased tail latency a little—there's a tradeoff.

[01:05] Anil: Quick note — the peering wasn't fully applied on our side, we discovered a missing route to the Redwood subnet that blocked the healthchecks from the pilot. I fixed the route table but still need to confirm NAT gateway egress rules for the runtime image pull.

[01:25] Maya: Okay thanks, Anil. Can you paste the subnet IDs and the current NACL and security group in the shared doc after the call? That will help us validate the allowlist.

[01:36] Anil: Yep, I'll do that.

[01:40] Karen: Also want to call out security — we need to see KMS integration details and confirm that keys are customer-managed. Where are we on that?

[01:50] Maya: Good question. We covered this in the security pack, but I'll re-share the specific KMS integration notes. For the Private deployment we support customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS or a BYOK HSM; audit logs are shipped to your CloudWatch account or S3 as configured. I'll attach the SOC2 cert link as well.

[02:12] Sara: Perfect, that helps. On the performance spreadsheet — Liam, you had a row that looked like weird spikes around 3pm local, is that an artifact?

[02:22] Liam: Yeah that was a noisy run — we had intermittent CPU steal on the host during that test. I traced it back to a mis-scheduled backup job on the host; we've pinned the CPU and re-ran the test. The cleaned numbers are the ones in the 'clean' tab.

[02:44] Maya: Great. For the upgrade to runtime v1.0 — what's required from BluePeak to make that smooth? Liam?

[02:52] Liam: From a networking perspective, nothing new other than the peering and the allowlist for the new control-plane endpoints. Runtime-wise, v1.0 includes an updated kernel selection path and a minor protocol change in how we negotiate streaming chunks — we do backward compatibility checks but we recommend a rolling upgrade across nodes to avoid a full outage. We'll supply a detailed step-by-step and a container image that you can test in a staging subnet.

[03:18] Anil: Does v1.0 require any config changes to the ALB or NLB listeners?

[03:24] Liam: No listener changes expected; if you're using TLS with client certs we'd need to drop in the new cert thumbprint into the allowlist. Also if you have strict IP-based allowlists you need to add the new control-plane IPs — I'll share those.

[03:42] Karen: What's the rollback plan if we see a regression after the upgrade?

[03:47] Maya: We do canary by default. The plan is: deploy v1.0 to a single AZ, monitor steady-state for 30–60 minutes, then extend. If we see regression, we can fail back to pinned v0.9.3 and we'll preserve the KV cache snapshots so warm-up is faster.

[04:06] Sara: About the KV cache — is the cache snapshotting cross-AZ aware? We saw warm-up penalties when traffic moved AZs.

[04:14] Liam: The cache snapshots are per-instance by default. For cross-AZ warm starts you can enable the optional shared cache layer; that requires provisioning a small Redis cluster in your VPC and a tiny config change. It's an add-on; we can show numbers for cost vs latency benefit.

[04:34] Anil: That Redis add-on would require us to open extra ports between AZs; worries about security and egress cost. Could we instead accept higher cold start and optimize routing?

[04:46] Maya: That's a fine tradeoff—if your workload is mostly single-AZ we can hold off on shared cache. If you need multi-AZ high availability with fast warm-ups, Redis is the better option. We'll put numbers in the benchmark.

[05:00] Sara: For the benchmark, are we running the 50k token run this week? I can schedule it but wanted to confirm the exact test harness.

[05:08] Liam: Use the 'long-form-latency' harness in the shared repo, set concurrency to 4, run 3 iterations, capture p50/p95/p99, and record token cost. There's a spreadsheet link in the drive — I pasted it in the calendar invite.

[05:24] Maya: Reminder: when you run it, try both batch_size 8 and 12 so we can see cost vs tail latency. Also include cold-start numbers.

[05:34] Sara: Will do.

[05:38] Anil: Back to peering — I found that our route table didn't include the /28 that Redwood gave us. I updated it but the pilot healthcheck is still failing intermittently; maybe security group on the host blocks ICMP so healthchecks show as degraded.

[05:58] Liam: Our healthchecks use TCP on port 8080, not ICMP — if SG blocks that it explains it. We'll add diagnostic logs to the control plane so you can see connection attempts.

[06:12] Maya: We'll also drop the allowlist IPs into the shared doc. Anil, once you paste your subnets we'll validate from our side.

[06:22] Karen: One more compliance question — BluePeak needs a written data residency statement. The pilot will process PHI in dev, so we need to ensure logs/audit don't leave the region.

[06:34] Maya: Understood. For Private deployments, control plane can be scoped to region and logs delivered to your S3 in-region. We'll share the exact retention/config options. I'll attach the data-residency snippet to the security packet.

[06:48] Sara: On cost — any early estimates if we switched to dedicated reserved capacity after pilot? I want ballpark per-node cost so I can model the 12-month burn.

[06:58] Maya: I can send a high-level estimate after we see your benchmark numbers; reserved capacity pricing depends on GPU type and commit—I'll include a couple of options: small reserved pool for predictable throughput and a burst pool for traffic spikes.

[07:12] Anil: For the upgrade window — we prefer weekends. Can you do the rolling upgrade on Saturday morning PST?

[07:18] Liam: Yes we can schedule Saturday 02:00–05:00 PST. It'll be a rolling upgrade across nodes with health probes. We'll provide a maintenance runbook beforehand.

[07:30] Karen: If we hit an issue and need Redwood on-call, what's the escalation path?

[07:36] Maya: For pilot customers we have SE on-call during the upgrade and a follow-the-sun escalation to our SREs. I'll include the on-call numbers in the runbook. For Dedicated customers there's a 24/7 SLA as an add-on.

[07:50] Sara: A couple of small transcriptions — in the spreadsheet one of the labels read 'K-V cash' which is kind of funny, it's KV cache.

[07:58] Liam: Haha yeah the auto transcript does that sometimes.

[08:04] Maya: Any blockers else?

[08:07] Anil: Just the peering confirm and the image pull egress rule. Once I confirm, should be clear.

[08:14] Sara: We'll run the 50k tonight after Anil finishes the route check and post results.

[08:20] Liam: Perfect. I'll re-run the same harness in our staging with v1.0 and paste the results so you can compare.

[08:28] Maya: I'll send the security docs and the updated network diagram with the control-plane IP list. Also will send the pricing estimate for reserved capacity.

[08:36] Karen: Thanks.

[08:38] Maya: Alright let's do a quick recap of action items — Anil will paste subnets and NACLs; Sara will run the 50k token run and update the spreadsheet; Liam will upload v1.0 test image and share control-plane IPs; I'll send security and pricing. We'll reconvene same time next week unless the upgrade is scheduled for Saturday, in which case we'll do a short post-upgrade check.

[09:05] Karen: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.

[09:09] Maya: End.
